questions.title: Astringent action
questions.question: A substance with a vasoconstrictor and protein-denaturing effect is said to have a/an ___ action.

explanations.A: Correct. An astringent is defined specifically by this combined action: vasoconstriction of superficial blood vessels together with denaturation (precipitation) of surface proteins. Together these two effects shrink and toughen exposed tissue, reduce secretions, and help control minor bleeding or oozing. This mechanism-based definition is what distinguishes an astringent from other topical agent categories.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An emollient softens and soothes the skin surface rather than constricting vessels or denaturing protein.
explanations.C: Incorrect. An antiseptic acts by killing or inhibiting microorganisms, not by vasoconstriction or protein denaturation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A rubefacient causes localized redness and warmth through vasodilation, the opposite of an astringent's vasoconstriction.

questions.learning_objective: State that combined vasoconstrictor and protein-denaturing action defines an astringent.

questions.title: Nasal route -- drug not suitable
questions.question: A systemic drug given through the nose may be any of the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Calcitonin is a small peptide that is in fact given intranasally for a systemic effect, so this is not the exception.
explanations.B: Correct. Heparin is a large, highly charged polysaccharide that cannot cross the nasal mucosa in clinically useful amounts, so it is never given by the intranasal route. Calcitonin, vasopressin and GnRH analogues are all small peptide or protein drugs that the nasal mucosa can absorb directly into the systemic circulation. This is why heparin is the exception among drugs otherwise given intranasally for a systemic effect.
explanations.C: Incorrect. GnRH analogues are small enough to be absorbed across the nasal mucosa for systemic action, so this is not the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Vasopressin is a small peptide routinely given intranasally, for example in diabetes insipidus, so this is not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: Identify heparin as unsuitable for intranasal systemic delivery, unlike small peptides such as calcitonin and vasopressin.

questions.title: MDI abbreviation
questions.question: MDI stands for:

explanations.A: Correct. MDI stands for metered dose inhaler, a pressurized device that delivers a fixed (metered) dose of drug with each actuation or puff. It is one of the two main classes of inhalation delivery device taught alongside dry powder inhalers. The propellant inside the canister aerosolises the drug so it can be inhaled into the lower airway.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This is not a recognised expansion of the abbreviation MDI; MDI specifically refers to the metered-dosing mechanism of the inhaler.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This is not a recognised pharmaceutical abbreviation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Micronisation describes particle size reduction, not the meaning of the MDI abbreviation itself.

questions.learning_objective: State that MDI stands for metered dose inhaler.

questions.title: SC route -- not an advantage
questions.question: Advantages of the subcutaneous (SC) route of administration include all of the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Steady absorption is a real advantage of the subcutaneous route, not the exception.
explanations.B: Correct. Irritant drugs are not suited to the subcutaneous route because the poorly vascularised subcutaneous tissue cannot quickly dilute or clear an irritant substance, risking local tissue damage. Steady absorption, tolerance of a moderate volume, and prolonged duration of action from a subcutaneous depot are all genuine advantages of the SC route. Because the question asks for the exception, allowing irritant drugs is the one item that is not actually an advantage of SC injection.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Tolerating an injected volume is presented as a genuine advantage in this question, not the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Prolonged duration of action from a subcutaneous depot is a genuine advantage, not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: State that irritant drugs are not suited to the subcutaneous route.

questions.title: Liniment -- alcoholic topical solution
questions.question: The following dosage form is an alcoholic solution for topical use:

explanations.A: Incorrect. A syrup is an oral sugar-based preparation, not a topical alcoholic solution.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An elixir is a sweetened hydroalcoholic solution taken orally, not applied topically.
explanations.C: Correct. A liniment is specifically an alcoholic solution intended for topical application, applied with rubbing to aid penetration and produce a mild counter-irritant effect. Syrup and elixir are both oral, not topical, preparations. Lotion, by contrast, is an aqueous, not alcoholic, topical solution applied without rubbing.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A lotion is an aqueous, not alcoholic, topical preparation, and is applied without rubbing.

questions.learning_objective: Identify liniment as the alcoholic topical solution among common dosage forms.

questions.title: SC route -- drug not best suited
questions.question: All of the following drugs are best given by the SC route EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Insulin is a classic example of a drug given by the subcutaneous route, so this is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Heparin (unfractionated or low-molecular-weight) is routinely given subcutaneously, so this is not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adrenaline is given subcutaneously (or intramuscularly) in emergencies such as anaphylaxis, so this is not the exception.
explanations.D: Correct. Hydrocortisone is not typically given by the subcutaneous route; it is more commonly administered orally, intramuscularly, intravenously or topically depending on indication. Insulin, heparin and adrenaline are all classic examples of drugs given subcutaneously. Because the question asks for the exception, hydrocortisone is the one drug not best suited to the SC route among this set.

questions.learning_objective: Identify hydrocortisone as not best given by the subcutaneous route, unlike insulin, heparin and adrenaline.

questions.title: Sublingual tablet definition
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: A spinhaler is used for liquid aerosols.
options.B: An ampoule is a multi-dose preparation for parenteral administration.
options.C: A spansule is a sugar-coated dosage form for masking the bad taste of a drug.
options.D: A sublingual tablet is a friable dosage form for rapid buccal disintegration.

explanations.A: Incorrect. A spinhaler delivers a dry powder for inhalation, not a liquid aerosol.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An ampoule is a single-dose, not multi-dose, sealed container for parenteral administration.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A spansule is a sustained-release capsule formulation, not a sugar-coated, taste-masking dosage form.
explanations.D: Correct. A sublingual tablet is specifically formulated to be friable, meaning it breaks down and disintegrates rapidly when placed under the tongue, allowing fast absorption across the buccal mucosa into the systemic circulation. This rapid disintegration is what makes the sublingual route suitable for drugs needing a fast onset of action, such as nitroglycerin in angina. The other three statements each misdescribe a different dosage form or device.

questions.learning_objective: Correctly define a sublingual tablet against common confusions with spinhaler, ampoule and spansule.

questions.title: Transdermal patch -- unsuitable use
questions.question: A transdermal patch is not suitable for the administration of:

options.B: Nitroglycerin for acute attack of angina

explanations.A: Incorrect. Clonidine is well suited to transdermal delivery for sustained blood pressure control, so this is not the exception.
explanations.B: Correct. A transdermal patch delivers a drug slowly across intact skin over hours, which makes it unsuitable whenever fast relief is needed, such as during an acute attack of angina. Nitroglycerin for an acute attack instead needs the fast-onset sublingual route; the transdermal patch form of nitroglycerin is used for prophylaxis, not for treating an attack already underway. Clonidine, estradiol and hyoscine are all genuinely well suited to transdermal delivery because they are used for steady, prolonged control rather than immediate relief.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Estradiol is well suited to transdermal delivery for sustained relief of menopausal symptoms, so this is not the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hyoscine is well suited to transdermal delivery for prevention of motion sickness, so this is not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: State that the transdermal route is unsuitable for treating an acute attack needing immediate relief.

questions.title: Aconitine toxicity
questions.question: Aconitine can lead to ___ without any anatomical lesions.

explanations.A: Correct. Aconitine is a highly toxic plant alkaloid whose overdose can cause death through severe cardiotoxicity and neurotoxicity, without producing any visible anatomical lesion at autopsy. This illustrates that a fatal drug effect need not correspond to structural tissue damage; the toxicity is purely functional. It is one of the classic examples used to teach that lethality and anatomical injury are not the same thing.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Aconitine toxicity is not characterised primarily by fever; its danger is cardiotoxicity and neurotoxicity that can be fatal without any anatomical lesion.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Aconitine does not characteristically cause ulceration; its toxic effect is functional, not a visible structural lesion.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Aconitine toxicity is not characterised by hepatic fibrosis; its danger is a functional cardiac and neurological effect.

questions.learning_objective: State that aconitine overdose can be fatal without leaving an anatomical lesion.

questions.title: Narcotic prescription requirements
questions.question: Regarding narcotic prescriptions:

options.B: Are used only for prescribing sedatives and hypnotics
options.D: Are written in duplicate on the ordinary prescription forms
options.E: The dose should be written in words, not numerals alone

explanations.A: Incorrect. Narcotic prescriptions specifically cannot be refilled without a fresh prescription, unlike some ordinary prescriptions.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Narcotic prescriptions are not restricted to sedatives and hypnotics; narcotic analgesics such as morphine are the classic example of a controlled drug requiring this type of prescription.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Narcotic drugs are prescription-only controlled substances by definition, not OTC (over-the-counter) drugs.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Narcotic prescriptions require a special controlled-drug prescription form, not an ordinary prescription form.
explanations.E: Correct. Narcotic (controlled-drug) prescriptions require the dose to be written out in words rather than left as numerals alone, as an anti-forgery safeguard, since numerals are easier to alter than written-out words. This is one of several extra safeguards placed on narcotic prescriptions to prevent forgery or diversion of controlled substances. The source prints this requirement as the correct answer among a list of otherwise-incorrect statements about narcotic prescriptions.

questions.learning_objective: State that a narcotic prescription's dose must be written in words as an anti-forgery safeguard.

questions.title: Dosage form needing rubbing
questions.question: Which of the following skin dosage forms needs rubbing after application?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A lotion is applied without rubbing, unlike a liniment.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An ointment is spread on the skin, not rubbed in the way a liniment is.
explanations.C: Correct. A liniment is an alcoholic topical solution that is specifically applied with rubbing, which both helps the drug penetrate the skin and produces a mild counter-irritant effect. Lotion, by contrast, is an aqueous solution applied without rubbing, and ointment, gel and cream are semisolid preparations spread rather than rubbed in. Rubbing-in is therefore the distinguishing application technique for a liniment among these five dosage forms.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A gel is spread on the skin rather than rubbed in.
explanations.E: Incorrect. A cream is spread on the skin rather than rubbed in.

questions.learning_objective: Identify liniment as the topical dosage form applied with rubbing.

questions.title: Heavy tea -- not a treatment for
questions.question: Heavy tea can be useful in the treatment of all of the following conditions EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Heavy tea's tannin content is genuinely useful in diarrhoea, so this is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Heavy tea's tannin content precipitates alkaloids, making it genuinely useful in alkaloid toxicity, so this is not the exception.
explanations.C: Correct. Heavy tea's high tannin content precipitates alkaloids and binds iron, which is why it is used in alkaloid toxicity and in chronic iron toxicity (hemochromatosis), and its astringent tannin action also helps in diarrhoea. Colic is a pain syndrome from smooth-muscle spasm or obstruction, a mechanism heavy tea's tannin content does not address. Because the question asks for the exception, colic is the condition heavy tea is not used to treat among this set.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Heavy tea's tannin content binds iron, making it genuinely useful in chronic iron toxicity, so this is not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: State that heavy tea treats alkaloid toxicity and iron toxicity via tannin action, not colic.

questions.title: Nasal decongestant -- not a feature
questions.question: Nasal decongestant drugs are characterized by all of the following features EXCEPT:

options.A: Should be applied to both sides of the nose at the same time
options.B: Can be used to open a blocked Eustachian tube
options.C: Are less preferred to oral medications in cases of the common cold
options.D: The head should be tilted backward during application

explanations.A: Correct. A topical nasal decongestant should be applied to one side of the nose at a time rather than both sides simultaneously, because treating both nostrils at once risks complete bilateral nasal obstruction if the mucosa reacts adversely, leaving the patient unable to breathe through the nose at all. Nasal decongestants genuinely can be used to open a blocked Eustachian tube, are genuinely less preferred than oral medications in the common cold, and the head genuinely should be tilted backward during application to aid distribution. Because the question asks for the exception, applying to both sides simultaneously is the one feature that is false.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Nasal decongestants can genuinely be used to help open a blocked Eustachian tube, so this is not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Nasal decongestants are genuinely less preferred than oral medications for the common cold, so this is not the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Tilting the head backward during application genuinely aids distribution of the decongestant, so this is not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: State that a nasal decongestant is applied to one nostril at a time, not both simultaneously.

questions.title: Depot preparation route
questions.question: A parenteral route suitable for depot preparation is the ___ route.

explanations.A: Correct. The intramuscular route is preferred for oily depot preparations because muscle's rich blood supply and larger tissue bed support a slow, sustained release of drug from an oily suspension injected into it. This gives prolonged action from a single injection, which is the defining purpose of a depot preparation. Intravenous injection bypasses any depot effect entirely, and intradermal and subcutaneous sites cannot hold the larger oily volumes an IM depot needs.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The intravenous route delivers the full dose directly into the circulation with no depot effect at all.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The intradermal site is too small and too close to the skin surface to serve as a depot.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The subcutaneous route's poorer blood supply and smaller tissue space make it less suited to a large oily depot than the intramuscular route.

questions.learning_objective: State that IM is the route of choice for depot preparations.

questions.title: Volatile oils -- not a use
questions.question: Volatile oils can be used for all of the following purposes EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Volatile oils are genuinely used as spasmolytics, so this is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Volatile oils are genuinely used as expectorants, so this is not the exception.
explanations.C: Correct. Volatile (essential) oils are used as spasmolytics, expectorants, carminatives and counter-irritants, but they are not used as laxatives; that action belongs to other pharmacological classes such as bulk-forming or stimulant laxatives. Because the question asks for the exception, laxative use is the one purpose volatile oils are not recognised for among this set. Each of the other four listed uses is a genuine, well-recognised application of volatile oils.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Volatile oils are genuinely used as carminatives, so this is not the exception.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Volatile oils are genuinely used as counter-irritants, so this is not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: State that volatile oils are not used as laxatives, unlike their genuine spasmolytic/expectorant/carminative/counter-irritant uses.

questions.title: Oral route characteristic
questions.question: What is characteristic of the oral route?

options.A: The sterilization of medicinal forms is obligatory
options.B: Absorption depends on GI tract secretion and motor function
options.E: A drug reaches the blood without passing through the liver

explanations.A: Incorrect. Sterilisation is not obligatory for oral dosage forms, since the oral route does not deliver the drug into sterile tissue.
explanations.B: Correct. Absorption of an orally administered drug genuinely depends on gastrointestinal secretion, which affects dissolution, and motor function, which affects transit time and contact with the absorptive surface, making it one of the oral route's defining and most variable characteristics. Sterilisation is not obligatory for oral dosage forms since they do not enter sterile tissue. Onset by the oral route is comparatively slow rather than fast, it is not the preferred route in an emergency, and an orally absorbed drug passes through the liver via the portal circulation rather than bypassing it.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The oral route has a comparatively slow onset of effect, not a fast one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The oral route is not preferred in an emergency, precisely because of its slow and variable onset.
explanations.E: Incorrect. An orally absorbed drug passes through the liver via the portal circulation and is subject to first-pass metabolism, rather than reaching the blood without passing through the liver.

questions.learning_objective: State that oral absorption depends on GI secretion and motor function.

questions.title: Sublingual nitroglycerin -- reason
questions.question: The main reason for administering nitroglycerin in angina pectoris by the sublingual route is:

options.B: It needs to be well mixed with saliva to be absorbed
options.E: It is too toxic to be given intravenously

explanations.A: Incorrect. Nitroglycerin's oral bioavailability problem is due to first-pass metabolism, not poor absorption from the gut itself.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Sublingual absorption occurs across the buccal mucosa, not because the drug needs to mix with saliva.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Avoiding gastric irritation is not the reason for choosing the sublingual route for nitroglycerin.
explanations.D: Correct. Nitroglycerin is given sublingually mainly to avoid first-pass hepatic metabolism, which would otherwise destroy most of an oral dose before it ever reached the systemic circulation. Sublingual absorption drains into the systemic veins directly, bypassing the portal circulation and liver entirely, which is also why the sublingual route gives a fast enough onset to relieve an acute angina attack. This is a specific pharmacokinetic reason, not related to gastric irritation, saliva mixing, or intravenous toxicity.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Nitroglycerin is not too toxic to be given intravenously; it is in fact also given by IV infusion in some clinical settings.

questions.learning_objective: State that sublingual nitroglycerin avoids first-pass hepatic metabolism.

questions.title: IV route -- disadvantage
questions.question: A disadvantage of the IV route of administration is:

options.A: Prolonged IV infusion usually leads to air embolism
options.C: Administration under aseptic technique can induce septicaemia
options.D: Extravasation outside the vein may lead to local necrosis
options.E: Administration in a neck vein may lead to brain damage

explanations.A: Incorrect. Air embolism is specifically linked to injection above the level of the heart, not simply to a prolonged infusion as such.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The IV route is in fact well suited to irritant drugs, since they are diluted directly in the bloodstream rather than concentrated at a tissue site.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Aseptic technique is meant to prevent, not induce, septicaemia.
explanations.D: Correct. If an IV needle or cannula slips outside the vein, the full, undiluted drug concentration is released directly into the surrounding tissue instead of being carried away and diluted by flowing blood, which can cause local tissue necrosis. This is one of the IV route's classic, technique-related hazards. The other listed options either describe the wrong mechanism or state something false about the IV route.
explanations.E: Incorrect. A properly performed neck vein injection is not characteristically linked to brain damage.

questions.learning_objective: State that extravasation of an IV injection can cause local tissue necrosis.

questions.title: MDI is not a dry powder inhaler
questions.question: One of the following inhalers is NOT a dry powder inhaler:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The turbohaler is a genuine dry powder inhaler device.
explanations.B: Correct. The metered dose inhaler (MDI) uses a pressurized propellant to aerosolise a liquid or suspended drug, which makes it fundamentally different from a dry powder inhaler. Turbohaler, spinhaler, discus and rotahaler are all genuine dry powder inhaler devices, activated by the patient's own inspiratory effort rather than a propellant. Because the question asks which device is NOT a dry powder inhaler, the MDI is the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The spinhaler is a genuine dry powder inhaler device.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The discus is a genuine dry powder inhaler device.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The rotahaler is a genuine dry powder inhaler device.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the MDI as pressurized/propellant-based and therefore not a dry powder inhaler.

questions.title: Cholestyramine classification
questions.question: Cholestyramine is a:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cholestyramine is not a nitrogenous, plant-derived alkaloid.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cholestyramine is not a sugar-aglycone glycoside.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cholestyramine is not a tannin.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cholestyramine is not a volatile oil.
explanations.E: Correct. Cholestyramine is a bile-acid-binding resin used to lower cholesterol by binding bile acids in the gut and promoting their excretion, which is why it is classified as a resin rather than an alkaloid, glycoside, tannin or volatile oil. Its resinous, ion-exchange structure is what allows it to bind bile acids in the intestinal lumen. This classification is purely structural, distinct from its clinical lipid-lowering use.

questions.learning_objective: Classify cholestyramine as a bile-acid-binding resin.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Curare is a genuine plant-derived alkaloid.

questions.title: IM route -- not a disadvantage
questions.question: Disadvantages of the IM route of administration include all of the following items EXCEPT:

options.A: Is more painful than the SC route

explanations.A: Correct. As printed in the source, being more painful than the SC route is the item that does not belong among IM's disadvantages in this question; the other four (infected abscesses, unsuitability for very large volumes, inadvertent intravenous injection, and difficulty of self-administration) are the disadvantages tested here. This printed key runs counter to the common teaching point that IM injections are usually described as more painful than SC ones, so it is kept exactly as printed rather than re-derived from general teaching, and the discrepancy is flagged rather than silently resolved. Students should treat the printed key as authoritative for this specific question even where it appears to conflict with a general teaching statement.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Infected abscesses are a genuine, recognised disadvantage of the IM route, so this is not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Unsuitability for very large volumes is a genuine disadvantage of the IM route relative to IV, so this is not the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Inadvertent intravenous injection during an intended IM injection is a genuine, recognised risk, so this is not the exception.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Difficulty of self-administration is a genuine, recognised disadvantage of the IM route compared with SC, so this is not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise IM's printed set of disadvantages per the source, distinct from a general painfulness claim.

questions.title: Glycoside -- not an example
questions.question: All of the following drugs are glycosides EXCEPT:

explanations.E: Correct. Insulin is a peptide hormone with no sugar-aglycone glycosidic structure, so it is not a glycoside despite being grouped in this question with genuine glycosides. questions.title: Parenteral administration -- general feature
questions.question: Regarding parenteral administration in general:

options.A: Generally results in a less accurate dosage than oral administration
options.B: The drug administered is usually rapidly eliminated by the kidney
options.C: Usually produces a more rapid response than oral administration
options.D: Cannot be used with unconscious patients
options.E: The drug administered can be easily retrieved in case of errors

explanations.A: Incorrect. Parenteral administration generally gives a more, not less, accurate dosage than oral administration, since it bypasses variable gut absorption.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Renal elimination rate is a property of the individual drug, not a general feature of the parenteral route.
explanations.C: Correct. Parenteral administration usually bypasses absorption delays inherent in the oral route, such as gastric emptying, intestinal transit and first-pass metabolism, so it typically produces a more rapid clinical response than oral administration for an equivalent dose. This onset-speed difference is exactly what the enteral/parenteral/topical route classification predicts. The other listed statements are each the reverse of the truth about the parenteral route in general.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Parenteral routes are in fact particularly useful in unconscious patients, since they do not require a co-operative gut.
explanations.E: Incorrect. A parenteral dose, once administered, generally cannot be retrieved in the event of an error.

questions.learning_objective: State that parenteral administration usually gives a faster response than oral administration.

questions.title: IM route characteristic
questions.question: What is characteristic of the intramuscular route of drug administration?

options.A: The action develops more slowly than with oral administration
options.B: Oily solutions are useful as a depot
options.C: The deltoid muscle is the most popular site
options.E: Only water solutions can be injected

explanations.A: Incorrect. Action by the intramuscular route generally develops faster than by the oral route, not more slowly.
explanations.B: Correct. Oily solutions injected intramuscularly form a depot in the muscle tissue from which the drug is released slowly over an extended period, taking advantage of muscle's tissue bulk and blood supply to sustain prolonged action from a single injection. This depot property is one of the intramuscular route's defining pharmaceutical characteristics. The other listed statements are each false as general claims about the IM route.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The gluteal region, not the deltoid, is generally the most commonly used large-muscle IM site.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Opportunity for hypertonic solution injection is not a defining characteristic of the IM route as such.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Both oily and aqueous solutions can be given intramuscularly, not water solutions alone.

questions.learning_objective: State that oily depot solutions are a defining use of the intramuscular route.

questions.title: Dosage form for a large skin area
questions.question: The most suitable dosage form which can be applied to a very large area of skin is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. A cream is thicker and greasier than a gel, making it less suited to covering a very large area.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A patch is sized for a small, fixed, localized area, not for broad coverage.
explanations.C: Correct. A gel's spreadable, non-greasy texture makes it the most suitable dosage form for covering a very large area of skin, since it spreads easily and does not leave the heavy residue that a cream or ointment would over a large surface. A patch is designed for a small, localized area of fixed size, not for broad coverage. Cream and ointment, while also topical, are less suited to large-area application than a gel because of their thicker, greasier consistency.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An ointment is even greasier and heavier than a cream, making it less suited to a very large area than a gel.

questions.learning_objective: Identify gel as the most suitable dosage form for a very large area of skin.

questions.title: IV route -- irritant drugs and large volumes
questions.question: A parenteral route suitable for irritant drugs and for large volumes is the ___ route.

explanations.A: Correct. The intravenous route delivers a drug directly into the flowing bloodstream, where it is immediately diluted, which is why irritant drugs are given intravenously rather than by a route where they would sit concentrated in tissue. The same direct-to-bloodstream delivery also allows large volumes, such as saline or glucose infusions, to be given safely by this route. Intramuscular, subcutaneous and intradermal sites cannot dilute an irritant drug the way flowing blood can, and none can accommodate the large volumes IV infusion can.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The intramuscular route cannot safely take either a highly irritant drug or a very large volume the way IV can.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The subcutaneous route is specifically unsuited to irritant drugs and large volumes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The intradermal route takes only a very small volume and is not used for irritant drugs.

questions.learning_objective: State that IV is the route suitable for irritant drugs and large volumes.

questions.title: MDI -- not a feature
questions.question: Metered dose inhalers are characterized by all of the following features EXCEPT:

options.A: Are not suitable for infants and neonates
options.D: Deliver a fixed dose per puff

explanations.A: Incorrect. MDIs are genuinely poorly suited to infants and neonates, who cannot reliably co-ordinate the breath-actuation technique required, so this is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. MDIs are genuinely pressurized devices, so this is not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. MDIs are genuinely portable devices, so this is not the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. MDIs genuinely deliver a fixed, metered dose per puff, so this is not the exception.
explanations.E: Correct. A metered dose inhaler's canister contains the active drug together with a propellant and other excipients needed to aerosolise and meter it, so it does not contain only the active drug. MDIs are genuinely pressurized, portable, deliver a fixed dose per puff, and are generally not well suited to infants and neonates. Because the question asks for the exception, containing only the active drug is the one feature that is false.

questions.learning_objective: State that an MDI canister contains propellant/excipients in addition to the active drug.

questions.title: Eye drop discard timing
questions.question: Discard eye drops after ___ weeks from the date the bottle had been opened.

explanations.A: Correct. Once a multidose eye drop bottle is opened, the standard dispensing rule is to discard it 4 weeks (one month) after the opening date, regardless of how much solution remains or what the unopened-bottle expiry date states. This rule exists because opening the bottle breaks the sterile seal and exposes the solution to repeated contact and ambient contamination with each use. The 4-week window limits the risk of ocular infection from a contaminated multidose container.
explanations.B: Incorrect. One week is shorter than the standard discard window for an opened multidose eye drop bottle.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Eight weeks exceeds the standard discard window and would risk using a contaminated solution.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Twelve weeks substantially exceeds the standard discard window and would risk using a contaminated solution.

questions.learning_objective: State the 4-week discard rule for an opened multidose eye drop bottle.

questions.title: Parenteral route -- pick the correct one
questions.question: Pick out the parenteral route of drug administration:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Inhalation is a respiratory-mucosal route, not the parenteral route being asked for here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Sublingual administration is conventionally classed with the enteral/oromucosal routes, not as parenteral.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Rectal administration uses the gastrointestinal tract and is an enteral, not parenteral, route.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Oral administration uses the gastrointestinal tract and is the classic enteral, not parenteral, route.
explanations.E: Correct. Intramuscular injection delivers the drug directly into muscle tissue, bypassing the gastrointestinal tract entirely, which is the defining feature of a parenteral route. Oral and rectal administration both use the gastrointestinal tract and so are enteral, not parenteral. Sublingual administration is conventionally classed with the enteral/oromucosal routes rather than as parenteral, and inhalation is a distinct respiratory-mucosal route, so intramuscular injection is the one clearly parenteral route among this set.

questions.learning_objective: Identify intramuscular injection as a parenteral route, unlike oral, rectal, sublingual or inhaled administration.

questions.title: Atropine sulfate solubility
questions.question: Atropine sulfate is soluble in ___.

explanations.A: Correct. Atropine sulfate is the salt form of the alkaloid atropine, and converting the free-base alkaloid to its sulfate salt makes it soluble in water, unlike the free base itself. This water solubility is exactly why atropine is formulated and dispensed clinically as atropine sulfate rather than as the free base, allowing aqueous injectable and eye-drop preparations. Free-base alkaloids in general are insoluble in water, which is the whole reason clinically used alkaloid drugs are converted to salt forms.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Atropine sulfate, being an ionic salt, is not soluble in a non-polar oil such as olive oil.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Atropine sulfate, being an ionic salt, is not soluble in a non-polar solvent such as liquid paraffin.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Atropine sulfate, being an ionic salt, is not soluble in a non-polar organic solvent such as ether.

questions.learning_objective: State that atropine sulfate is water-soluble, unlike the free-base alkaloid.

questions.title: Not intended for local action
questions.question: Which of the following drugs is not intended for local action?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Boric acid lotion is applied for local antiseptic/soothing action on the skin, not systemic effect.
explanations.B: Correct. A nitroglycerin tablet, despite resembling an ordinary oral solid dosage form, is placed sublingually specifically so the drug is absorbed into the systemic circulation to relieve angina through its action on the coronary and peripheral circulation, not for any local effect in the mouth. Boric acid lotion, Colgate toothpaste, Bradoral lozenges and Daktarin oral gel are all formulated and used for local action confined to the site of application. Because the question asks which drug is NOT intended for local action, the nitroglycerin tablet is the exception, acting systemically instead.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Colgate toothpaste acts locally on the teeth and gums, not systemically.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Bradoral lozenges act locally in the mouth and throat, not systemically.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Daktarin oral gel acts locally against oral fungal infection, not systemically.

questions.learning_objective: Identify a sublingual nitroglycerin tablet as acting systemically, unlike locally-acting lotion/paste/lozenge/gel preparations.
